inspection.coder: lead AI research engineer (Claude); single-coder visual inspection of thumbnails and three nearest neighbours
inspection.scope: Top 24 category conflicts from DINOv2-L raw neighbours (>=7/10 agreement), before the Lithotomes remapping
inspection.status: observational coding; not expert review; one coder; no inter-rater agreement measured

codes.label_mapping_error: Our coarse category mapping was wrong (Lithotomes = stone forceps); image neighbours were correct. Also exposes the existing rule that assigns cutting to these forceps.
codes.shared_lever_mechanism: Instrument reuses the crossed-lever forceps/plier mechanism for a different action (spreading/dilating); whole-form similarity reflects mechanism, not function.
codes.taxonomy_boundary: Catalog distinguishes categories (clamp vs grasping forceps) that share the ring-handled hinged form; a naming granularity question, not an error.
codes.shared_large_fenestrated_blades: Large paired fenestrated or curved blades resemble obstetric forceps; similar form across different named uses.
codes.archaeological_incompleteness: Object lacks the part that defined its catalog type (e.g. a lost iron blade); remaining handle resembles probes.
codes.resolution_limit: Long thin shaft whose working end is too small to resolve in the thumbnail; forceps, probes and lancets become indistinguishable.
codes.photographic_style: Neighbours share a distinctive photograph layout (scale bar, number card, black frame) rather than form.
codes.possible_catalog_image_mismatch: The catalog term and the visible object appear inconsistent; needs source check (possible wrong image or term).
codes.handle_without_blade: Detachable-blade handle photographed apart from its blade resembles flat tweezers.

changelog: 1.0.0: thresholds and states fixed before outputs were generated.

1.1.0 (post hoc, after inspecting 1.0.0 outputs; thresholds unchanged): image hypotheses withheld for depictions, documents, kits and other non-single units (a portrait and photographs of forceps had received function hypotheses); added flags atypical_for_catalog_category (image hypothesis for a function carried by <10% of the catalog category, e.g. specula sharing the forceps lever form) and typical_for_catalog_category (conflict against a function carried by >50% of the category, e.g. dental forceps and extraction: use is not visible in form).
1.1.1: removed unused min_neighbour_labelled (neighbours are always drawn from labelled records, k=15); no behaviour change.

modern_analogs.note: Nearest contemporary photographs by DINOv2-L raw cosine; family-level visual analogs, not descent or verified equivalent use.

status_definitions.observation: directly measured on this corpus with the stated controls
status_definitions.inference: an interpretation supported by several observations; alternative explanations remain
status_definitions.speculation: a hypothesis worth testing; not supported by current evidence alone

findings.evaluation_note: Targets are weak: a coarse catalog category (6 classes, 2,545 records) and rule-based function labels, both derived from catalog text. They are non-circular for image and shape representations only. No expert-reviewed labels exist. Chance category P@10 = 0.345; random cross-museum P@10 = 0.377. Intervals are 95% group-bootstrap (1,000 resamples).

findings.title: Pretrained vision models recover catalog categories, and the best transfer across museums
findings.statement: Frozen DINOv2-L on raw photographs retrieves same-category neighbours far above chance and transfers across museums better than the earlier ResNet18 and hand-crafted outline baselines.
evidence: DINOv2-L raw: category P@10 0.844 [0.834, 0.854]; cross-museum P@10 0.737 [0.723, 0.750] vs random 0.377.
Versus outline multiblock baseline: cross-museum P@10 +0.186 [0.174, 0.199]; versus ResNet18: category P@10 +0.087.

Held-out museum linear probe, macro-F1 (DINOv2-L vs ResNet18): Boerhaave -> Region Skane 0.65 vs 0.53 (5 shared classes, 462 test records); Region Skane -> Boerhaave 0.78 vs 0.49 (4 classes, 1,569 records).
caveats: Targets are catalog terms, not verified types or uses.

findings.title: Raw-photo embeddings carry museum photography signatures
findings.statement: Background colour, brightness and image resolution are linearly decodable from photo embeddings, and same-category neighbours come disproportionately from the same museum.
evidence: Background green channel R^2 from DINOv2-L raw 0.83; from the silhouette view 0.05.
Within-category same-museum enrichment of top-10 neighbours: 1.59x (DINOv2-L raw), 1.38x (silhouette), 1.27x (outline baseline).
Image size is decodable even from catalog text embeddings (R^2 ~0.9): resolution is effectively a museum marker.
caveats: Region Skane objects photographed on green keep a faint halo after background removal; only the silhouette view is fully background-free.

findings.title: Photography alone predicts category inside a museum but not across museums
findings.statement: Eight photographic nuisance descriptors reach category P@10 0.537 (chance 0.345) but exactly random cross-museum P@10 (0.376 vs 0.377) and near-zero held-out-museum transfer, so the cross-museum success of image models is not explained by these descriptors.
evidence: Photo-nuisance control: P@10 0.537 [0.526, 0.548]; cross-museum P@10 0.376 [0.365, 0.389]; museum transfer macro-F1 0.09 / 0.25.
caveats: Other photographic cues not captured by eight descriptors (framing, scale cards) may still contribute; see disagreement code 'photographic_style'.

findings.title: For pure 2-D outline, deep models add nothing over interpretable shape descriptors
findings.statement: With background and texture removed, deep silhouette embeddings match but do not beat the existing hand-crafted outline distance at cross-museum retrieval. The value of deep models here comes from internal structure, material and shading in the photograph, which is also where the confounds live.
evidence: Cross-museum P@10 difference vs outline: DINOv2-L silhouette +0.006 [-0.004, 0.017]; DINOv2-B +0.005 [-0.005, 0.016]; SigLIP 2 +0.013 [0.003, 0.024]; CLIP -0.014 [-0.025, -0.004].
caveats: Silhouettes from thumbnails fill small holes and lose thin parts.

findings.title: Photography-randomised adaptation reduces museum signatures without losing retrieval, but does not beat the larger frozen model on an unseen museum
findings.statement: Fine-tuning DINOv2-B against catalog text with background compositing and resolution randomisation improves its own backbone and lowers decodability of background and museum, consistently over three seeds. On an entirely unseen museum it equals, not exceeds, frozen DINOv2-L.
evidence: Unseen Region Skane (model never saw it): cross-museum P@10 +0.046 vs frozen DINOv2-B (seed range 0.041-0.051; seed-17 CI [0.029, 0.062]); +0.003 vs frozen DINOv2-L (seed-17 CI [-0.011, 0.019]).
Same-museum enrichment on that set: 1.56x (adapted) vs 1.79x (DINOv2-B) and 1.75x (DINOv2-L).
Compositing ablation: background R^2 0.33 vs 0.47 without compositing (test split); category retrieval unchanged (paired difference CI spans zero).
caveats: Adaptation is supervised by text that names the category, so its in-category gain (+0.054 test P@10) is expected rather than a discovery.

findings.title: Working-end crops alone do not improve fine distinctions at thumbnail resolution
findings.statement: Contrary to the part-based hypothesis from the affordance literature, best-matching end crops retrieve fine Boerhaave subtypes (artery / dental / stone / polyp forceps, nasal / ear specula) worse than the whole object; combining them adds a small overall gain.
evidence: Fine-subtype P@10 (31 subtypes, 988 records): ends minus whole -0.073 [-0.087, -0.059]; whole+ends minus whole +0.013 [0.006, 0.020]; within the same coarse category +0.007 [-0.000, 0.014].
caveats: Ends of thin instruments are a few pixels wide in thumbnails; the test should be repeated on full-resolution images before rejecting the idea.

findings.title: Image disagreements expose catalog-mapping errors, shared mechanisms and resolution limits
findings.statement: Records whose image neighbours contradict the catalog category are informative. Visual coding of the top 24 found two label-mapping errors (all 34 'Lithotomes' are stone forceps, and the existing rules assign them 'cutting'), five specula that reuse the crossed-lever forceps mechanism to spread rather than close, four taxonomy-boundary cases, four large fenestrated-blade look-alikes, five resolution limits, one blade-less Roman scalpel, one photographic-style cluster and one possible catalog/image mismatch.
evidence: 185 conflicts before and 168 after correcting the Lithotomes mapping (rule: >=7 of 10 DINOv2-L neighbours share another category).
META-002404 'seaweed' carries a mirrored copy of the photograph of META-002288 'grain pliers' (near-duplicate audit, cosine >= 0.98).
caveats: Single coder, thumbnails only, no inter-rater agreement; codes are inspection notes, not expert adjudication.

findings.title: Shared mechanism, not shared function, often drives whole-form similarity
findings.statement: Specula and dilators built on forceps-like crossed levers sit among forceps in every image space, and image-neighbour transfer then proposes 'gripping' for them. Image similarity therefore groups instruments by mechanism and construction; mapping it to function requires knowing whether the mechanism closes, spreads or cuts.
evidence: 'speculum_dilator -> grasping_forceps' is the third most frequent conflict pair (22 records).
92 image hypotheses are flagged atypical_for_catalog_category; 40 are specula receiving 'gripping'.
caveats: Direction of action (closing vs spreading) is rarely visible in a single still photograph.

findings.title: Multi-channel hypotheses: mostly corroboration, a small set of new candidates and explicit conflicts
findings.statement: Combining source text, existing rules and calibrated photo and silhouette neighbour channels yields 147 image-only function hypotheses for single-object records and 74 rule-image conflicts, each with evidence and flags. Image-channel agreement with existing rules is well calibrated on held-out groups (test ECE <= 0.051), but agreement with rules is not correctness of use.
evidence: State counts per function in experiments.hypotheses.state_counts; 69 image hypotheses are photography-dependent (photo supports, silhouette does not); 38 have silhouette agreement; 92 are atypical for their catalog category (49 on specula, 40 of them 'gripping').
Known channel failure: dental forceps flagged against 'extraction' (use is not visible in form; flag typical_for_catalog_category).
caveats: No independent validation yet; precision of the new hypotheses is unknown.

findings.title: Multilingual zero-shot search works on Dutch and Swedish catalog vocabulary
findings.statement: SigLIP 2 retrieves held-out images from short English, Dutch and Swedish terms well above base rate, better than the adapted model, whose text head learned full catalog descriptions rather than short queries. Zero-shot affordance prompts ('hinged jaws', 'spoon-shaped end') are only weakly informative about functions.
evidence: Test precision@20 over 18 scored queries: SigLIP 2 0.72 (en 0.78, nl 0.67, sv 0.71) vs adapted 0.57; base rate 0.19.
Affordance prompts vs weak function labels: mAP 0.39 (SigLIP 2 raw) vs prevalence 0.19, against 0.91 for image-neighbour transfer; extraction and scraping near chance.
Image -> own catalog text R@1: 0.07 zero-shot SigLIP 2 vs 0.26 adapted (test split).
caveats: Queries are dictionary terms chosen in advance; a small query set.

findings.title: Similarity is not lineage
findings.statement: None of these representations can distinguish inherited design from convergent solutions to the same mechanical problem. Neighbour structure is a candidate generator for comparisons that must then be tested with dated, documented maker/designer links and coded characters.
evidence: Mechanism-driven groupings (F8), photography-driven clustering (F2) and catalog-term dependence (text rows) all produce strong similarity without implying descent.

findings.title: Possible functional convergence between unrelated traditions
findings.statement: Cross-category silhouette look-alikes (e.g. blades vs. probes, clamps vs. grasping forceps across Dutch, Swedish and ethnographic collections) are candidate cases of convergent form that merit expert comparison of working ends and wear.
evidence: 200 closest cross-category silhouette pairs are exported for inspection (experiments.disagreements.cross_category_lookalikes).

findings.title: Image representations transfer to an independently curated external corpus, mostly through photographs rather than outlines
findings.statement: A probe trained only on internal DINOv2-L features assigns external Wikimedia Commons and Wellcome Collection photographs to four shared families (forceps, blade, probe, speculum) well above chance, best for contemporary photographs; the silhouette-only probe fails externally, where the segmentation was never validated.
evidence: Raw view: balanced accuracy 0.61, macro-F1 0.60 (chance 0.25; majority accuracy 0.56; n = 1,248 external photographs).
By era (balanced accuracy): contemporary 0.83 (n = 62), historical 0.55 (n = 589).
Silhouette view: balanced accuracy 0.36.
Nearest contemporary analogs by internal category: grasping forceps -> forceps 555, needle holder 296, scissors 204; specula -> speculum 107; blades -> scalpel/knife 97 (top-5 vote winners).
caveats: External class labels are weak (titles and categories).
Only 171 contemporary reference photographs (177 contemporary images), largely one photographer; analogs are family-level visual neighbours, not descent or equivalent use.
External segmentation quality is unverified; the silhouette failure may be segmentation, not shape.

next_experiments.title: Expert pair judgments
next_experiments.detail: Collect blinded graded judgments (shape / mechanism / function relevance) for ~300 query-neighbour pairs sampled across methods and museums, to replace weak-label proxies with Recall@k and nDCG; measure expert-expert agreement as the ceiling.

next_experiments.title: Full-resolution images
next_experiments.detail: Request or harvest full-resolution Boerhaave and Region Skane photographs and repeat the working-end experiment (F6), where thumbnails are the binding limit.

next_experiments.title: Validate new hypotheses
next_experiments.detail: Review a stratified sample of the 147 image hypotheses and 74 conflicts; estimate precision per state and flag; check the Lithotomes rule and META-002404 against the museum source.

next_experiments.title: Mechanism-aware labels
next_experiments.detail: Code mechanism (closing lever, spreading lever, spring, screw, fixed blade) separately from function and test whether image similarity predicts mechanism better than function (F8).

next_experiments.title: Leave-one-museum-out at scale
next_experiments.detail: Repeat adaptation holding out each museum with enough records, and add an adversarial museum-invariance objective compared against compositing alone.

next_experiments.title: External modern-instrument analogs
next_experiments.detail: Done in part (F13): expand the contemporary reference set beyond one photographer (manufacturer catalogues with permissive licences), validate external segmentation, and judge analogs with experts.

next_experiments.title: Historical relationship tests
next_experiments.detail: Combine dated designer/maker attributions with coded characters to test descent hypotheses explicitly, using similarity only to propose candidates.
